label: LocalDB
description: SQL Server LocalDB instances for local applications and automated tests, including instance creation, connection strings, and database deployment.
reason: LocalDB is a database technology; load-testing describes measuring systems under concurrent demand.

label: Continuous Integration
description: Automating builds and tests as changes enter a shared codebase, including build definitions, prerequisite setup, and repeatable execution environments.
reason: Build automation is unrelated to separating interface roles.

label: Azure
description: Deploying and operating applications on Microsoft Azure, including service configuration, role startup, storage, and execution environments.
reason: Azure is a specific cloud platform; architecture describes system organization independently of platform.

label: Windows Impersonation
description: Executing work under a different Windows identity through logon tokens and impersonation contexts, including privileges and identity lifetime.
reason: Windows identity and privilege handling is distinct from ownership of test resources.

label: MSMQ
description: Microsoft Message Queuing for passing work between processes through local or remote queues, including installation and queue-based processing.
reason: MSMQ is a messaging service, not language-model infrastructure.

label: Background Processing
description: Moving work beyond the initiating request into another execution context, with explicit handoff, processing responsibilities, and completion behavior.
reason: Process handoff and deferred execution are separate subjects from contracts around external libraries.

label: REST
description: Designing and consuming resource-oriented HTTP APIs through resource identifiers, method semantics, representations, and response status codes.
reason: REST describes API interaction semantics rather than verification practices.

label: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing
description: The HTTP mechanism through which a server permits browser requests from another origin, including origin headers, preflight requests, and allowed methods or headers.
reason: Browser origin permissions are unrelated to internal code reorganization. JSONP remains a separate subject.

label: jQuery
description: Using jQuery to work with browser elements, events, attached data, and Ajax requests.
reason: jQuery is a browser JavaScript library, unrelated to the Jev model.

label: HTTP Method Override
description: Carrying an intended HTTP method in a header on another request method, then translating it before dispatch to an application handler.
reason: HTTP method transport and dispatch differ from programming-language method contracts.

label: JavaScript
description: Material specific to JavaScript, or illustrated with JavaScript examples.
reason: The source contains JavaScript, without TypeScript syntax or type checking.

label: JSON
description: Representing structured data with JSON and converting between JSON text and application objects, including serialization and response handling.
reason: JSON is a data representation used across languages, not a Python-specific subject.

label: HttpClient
description: The .NET HttpClient API for sending HTTP requests and consuming responses, including request content, headers, asynchronous calls, and typed data conversion.
reason: HttpClient is an HTTP client API, not a test ownership or cleanup practice.

label: JSONP
description: Returning JSON inside a JavaScript callback so browser clients can consume script responses across origins, including callback selection and endpoint exposure.
reason: JSONP is a browser response technique, not language-specific Python material; it is also distinct from JSON representation and CORS headers.

label: Self-Hosting
description: Running a network service inside an application's own process, with explicit listener configuration, routing, startup, and lifetime management.
reason: Service hosting and lifetime are separate from parallel model judgments.

label: Quartz for ASP.NET
description: Shiv Kumar's ASP.NET page-composition framework, where Builders assemble view objects and HTML templates into dynamic pages.
reason: This is a named page-composition framework, unrelated to transport observation. It must not be confused with the Quartz.NET scheduler.

label: HTML Templates
description: Reusable HTML structures whose placeholders receive application data or rendered views, including template selection and separation from rendering code.
reason: HTML rendering templates are distinct from the Template Method software design pattern.

label: ASP.NET WebForms
description: Building and configuring ASP.NET WebForms applications, including application startup, project structure, and integration with HTTP services.
reason: WebForms names a specific web framework, not behavior-preserving code reorganization.

label: Roslyn
description: The .NET compiler platform exposes syntax trees, symbols, and semantic information for tools that inspect, transform, or generate source code.
reason: Transport observation does not cover compiler APIs or source analysis.

label: Syntax Highlighting
description: Classifying source-code tokens and rendering them with distinct visual styles, including the relationship between syntactic structure and semantic information.
reason: Asynchronous enumeration does not cover source-code rendering.

label: Visitor Pattern
description: Applying operations while visiting elements of an object structure, with separate handling for the kinds of elements encountered.
reason: Iteration supplies traversal; Visitor separates operations according to the visited element.

label: Connected Devices
description: Physical devices connected to computers or networks, with software interfaces that let applications read their state or control their behavior.
reason: Reviewing code does not cover networked hardware and device APIs.

label: Sandboxing
description: Restricting an application's access to system resources and exposing permitted capabilities through controlled interfaces and permissions.
reason: Failure handling does not cover execution permissions or resource isolation.

label: WCF
description: Windows Communication Foundation services and clients, including contracts, transport bindings, endpoints, hosting, metadata exchange, and diagnostics.
reason: Test substitution does not cover the WCF communication framework.

label: Service Proxies
description: Client-side objects that expose a remote service's operations and translate local calls into messages sent through a transport.
reason: A service locator selects collaborators; a service proxy invokes a remote service.

label: ASP.NET
description: Building web applications with ASP.NET, including request processing, handlers, controllers, responses, and framework behavior.
reason: Class organization does not cover the ASP.NET web application framework.

label: HTTP
description: HTTP request and response behavior, including methods, headers, connections, content, and client-server communication.
reason: Testing does not cover HTTP protocol behavior or request construction.

label: Asynchronous Programming Model
description: The .NET Asynchronous Programming Model exposes Begin and End method pairs, IAsyncResult, callbacks, and state for asynchronous operations.
reason: The specific Begin/End API contract also applies to asynchronous computation and deserves its own subject.

label: LINQ
description: Language Integrated Query operations over data, including filtering, projection, joins, grouping, and the relationship between query and method syntax.
reason: Class design does not cover sequence queries and their operators.

label: Parallel Programming
description: Dividing computational work so multiple processors or cores execute it at the same time, with attention to partitioning, scheduling, synchronization, and overhead.
reason: Abstraction levels concern responsibility boundaries; parallel programming concerns simultaneous computation. Concurrency overlaps but is broader than distributing computation across cores.

label: WMI
description: Windows Management Instrumentation exposes management information about Windows systems through queryable classes and properties.
reason: Naming does not cover Windows management APIs.

label: CPU Hardware
description: Processor characteristics such as physical packages, cores, logical processors, instruction-set architecture, and address width.
reason: A language tag does not identify processor hardware as a subject.

label: URL Encoding
description: Representing data in URL components through percent encoding, with attention to reserved characters, unreserved characters, and form-encoding conventions.
reason: Concurrent operations do not cover URL character representation.

label: Windows Services
description: Background services managed by Windows, including service discovery, lifecycle commands, status changes, and programmatic control.
reason: Language interfaces do not cover operating-system service management.

label: Process Management
description: Launching and controlling operating-system processes, collecting standard output and errors, waiting for completion, and interpreting exit status.
reason: Reporting application progress differs from managing external process lifecycles and streams.

label: SQL Server
description: Microsoft SQL Server databases, including SQL commands, storage features, administration, and application integration.
reason: Dependency selection does not cover a database platform. Data Access describes application boundaries rather than database administration.

label: Identity Columns
description: Database columns whose numeric values are generated from a seed and increment, including how insertion and reseeding affect subsequent values.
reason: Reducing language-model context does not cover generated database identifiers.

label: Duplicate Detection
description: Finding repeated values or records under an explicitly chosen comparison key, including grouping matches and retaining the records that share that key.
reason: A template method organizes behavior; duplicate detection identifies repeated data.

label: Serialization
description: Converting objects and sequences into representations that can be stored or transmitted, and reconstructing values from those representations. Contracts determine member names, data shape, and stream handling.
reason: Verification establishes evidence; serialization transforms data representations.

label: DataReaders
description: Reading result sets sequentially through ADO.NET DataReaders. Typed wrappers, connection lifetime, and the choice between streaming rows and materializing objects shape their use.
reason: A DataReader is a specific result-reading API; Data Manager describes an architectural responsibility.

label: Debugging
description: Investigating unexpected application behavior with diagnostic tools, traces, and observed execution to identify its cause.
reason: Delegates are a language mechanism. Debugging names the investigation practice, which structured logging can support but does not cover.

label: Web Performance
description: How quickly websites deliver responses and become usable in a browser. Server processing, transferred resources, caching, and measurement all contribute to the result.
reason: Public Surface concerns component contracts. Web performance also extends beyond the concurrent-demand measurements covered by Load Testing.

label: Blogging
description: The tools and workflows for writing, editing, and publishing blog posts, including blog engines and their authoring interfaces.
reason: Blogging concerns publishing articles; structured logging records application events.

label: MetaWeblog API
description: An XML-RPC interface for creating and editing blog posts, retrieving categories, and uploading media. Blog engines implement its operations so compatible authoring clients can publish to them.
reason: MetaWeblog is a concrete publishing protocol unrelated to requirements traceability.

label: Code Generation
description: Producing source code from metadata, models, or templates. Generators turn a repeatable structure into code while keeping the inputs and generated responsibilities explicit.
reason: Code Review evaluates code; code generation produces it.

label: ADO.NET
description: .NET data-access APIs for connections, commands, parameters, readers, adapters, and in-memory tables. Provider abstractions support working with different database engines.
reason: ADO.NET is a data-access API family rather than a performance-testing practice.

label: Stored Procedures
description: Named database operations that accept parameters and execute commands close to the stored data. Their result sets and parameters provide contracts for application data access.
reason: Stored procedures concern database operations, not parsing contracts.

label: OAuth
description: Delegating access to protected resources through provider-issued credentials and tokens. Applications follow an authorization flow and use the resulting access token for permitted requests.
reason: OAuth is an authorization protocol, unrelated to load testing.

label: Reflection
description: Inspecting types and members at runtime and invoking capabilities that are not fixed in the calling code. In .NET, reflection also supports generating executable methods through Reflection.Emit.
reason: Reflection is a runtime mechanism; refactoring changes code organization.

label: Request Binding
description: Mapping HTTP form fields and query parameters into typed values or objects. Binders define conversion, defaults, and how multiple incoming fields populate a model.
reason: Request binding transforms incoming HTTP data; requirements traceability connects requirements to evidence.

label: Type Conversion
description: Transforming a value from one representation or data type into another, including parsing text, handling numeric formats, and converting collections or custom objects.
reason: Type Casting covers checks and casts based on runtime type compatibility. This subject centrally concerns parsing and constructing different value representations.

label: Razor
description: Razor combines C# expressions and control flow with text templates. It supports ASP.NET views and layouts as well as hosted template generation outside a web application.
reason: Razor is a template engine and syntax; refactoring describes restructuring code.

label: Model-View-Controller
description: An application structure that separates models, presentation, and the controllers coordinating interactions. Implementations determine how data and control pass between those roles.
reason: Model evaluation concerns language-model decisions, not the MVC application structure.

label: File Upload
description: Transferring files from clients to servers, including file selection, multipart requests, progress feedback, and completion or failure handling.
reason: Service Locator is an architectural role, not a file-transfer operation.

label: XMLHttpRequest
description: The browser API for sending HTTP requests and receiving responses from scripts, including request bodies, upload events, and asynchronous completion.
reason: Testing does not identify this browser HTTP API.

label: Web Browsers
description: Browser behavior, standards support, performance, and the controls people use to navigate and interact with websites.
reason: Try-Parse is a parsing contract, not a browser subject.

label: User Interface Design
description: Arranging controls, content, navigation, and feedback around the tasks people need to perform.
reason: Service Interface Layer describes a system boundary, not the interface presented to a person.

label: Flash Player
description: Adobe's historical runtime for browser multimedia and interactive content, including video playback, SWF execution, and desktop or mobile integration.
reason: Factory Pattern is unrelated to the multimedia runtime.

label: Video Codecs
description: Video encoding and decoding formats, including their compression, picture quality, playback support, and hardware requirements.
reason: Service Locator does not cover video compression or decoding.

label: HTTP Range Requests
description: HTTP requests for selected portions of a resource, supporting partial downloads and seeking within media without transferring the entire file first.
reason: Progress reporting describes work already performed; range requests select the bytes to transfer.

label: Home Theater PC
description: Using a general-purpose computer with a television and audio system for media playback, browsing, and applications, including display connections and remote input.
reason: Load testing measures concurrent system demand, not a living-room computer setup.

label: Online Video
description: Delivering and watching video over the Internet, including picture quality, bandwidth, playback devices, and viewing experience.
reason: Configuration Provider is unrelated to Internet video delivery and viewing.

label: HTML5 Video
description: Native video playback through the HTML video element, including controls, poster images, browser behavior, and supported media formats.
reason: Class design does not cover the HTML video element or browser playback.

label: Video Posters
description: Representative images shown before video playback, including frame selection, custom thumbnails, and their presentation in video players.
reason: Idempotency describes repeated operations, not video preview images.

label: HTML Parsing
description: Reading HTML as a document structure to select elements and extract text, attributes, links, and other information.
reason: Try-Parse defines invalid-input return behavior; HTML parsing concerns document structure and extraction.

label: HtmlAgilityPack
description: A .NET library for loading and parsing HTML documents, navigating their nodes, and extracting information with selectors such as XPath.
reason: Strategy Pattern does not identify the HTML parsing library.

label: H.264
description: The AVC video coding standard, including compression and playback characteristics, implementation support, and licensing distinctions.
reason: Python is a programming language and does not cover the video coding standard.

label: CSS
description: Stylesheets that control web presentation, including layout, positioning, overflow, colors, typography, and visual states.
reason: C# does not cover stylesheet rules or web layout.

label: FTP
description: The File Transfer Protocol and its server configuration, including user access, directory isolation, and file-transfer permissions.
reason: Refactoring does not cover file-transfer protocols or server configuration.

label: Authentication
description: Establishing the identity of a user or client through credentials and configured identity providers before granting access.
reason: Test isolation concerns ownership of test state; authentication establishes identity.

label: ASP.NET Web API
description: The ASP.NET Web API framework for HTTP services, including ApiController routing, hosting, message handlers, formatters, and response construction.
reason: A web-service framework is distinct from the asynchronous language features it may use.
